findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. Because the two branches are OR'd, the cron deletes any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount > 1, not only SMS ones. Today only this SMS job increments retryCount, so the impact is latent. But any other job that starts using the column will have its reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron. Move the method filter outside the OR so it covers both branches.

findings.title: Threshold `gt: 1` deletes after two failures, but the failed reminder is also dropped from this run's remaining logic
findings.body: A reminder is deleted only on the next cron run after retryCount reaches 2. Meanwhile, retried reminders are not backed off at all, so each cron run (possibly every few minutes) counts as a retry. Two transient Twilio errors (rate limit, network blip) in consecutive runs permanently drop the reminder. The retry count therefore does not distinguish permanent failures (invalid number) from transient ones. The `gt: 1` magic number is also undocumented and does not clearly match the 'failed twice' wording in the description.

findings.title: Update inside catch can throw and abort the whole batch
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not itself guarded. If it throws (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently), the exception escapes the for-loop. The handler then fails with a 500 and every remaining reminder in the batch goes unprocessed. Wrap the update in its own try/catch or use `updateMany`.

findings.title: Reminders with no message or no sendTo never count as a retry
findings.body: The common failure case, such as an invalid or missing phone number (`sendTo` is null) or an empty message, fails the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` check. That branch has no else, so retryCount is never incremented and the reminder is retried on every cron run until scheduledDate. This is exactly the problem the PR is meant to fix. Also, `continue` for missing workflowStep/booking has no retry handling.

findings.title: Use atomic increment and consider an index
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses a value read earlier, so concurrent cron runs can lose increments. Use `{ increment: 1 }`. The new `retryCount` delete predicate is also OR'd with the existing indexed condition, so it can force a full table scan on WorkflowReminder, and the migration adds no index for it.
